lines.say: Hi! Could I come in on Wednesday afternoon?
lines.direction: Caller (on the phone): a little tentative and hopeful, slightly hushed — it's the middle of the night; relaxed, natural.
lines.speak: Oh, hi. Um, could I come in on Wednesday afternoon?

lines.say: Of course! I have 3 PM, or 4:30. Which one suits you better?
lines.direction: Ava: helpful and bright; a tiny beat after "Of course."; offers the two times naturally, a light upturn on "Which suits you better?"

lines.direction: Caller: pleased and relieved, a small smile in the voice.
lines.speak: Oh, three o'clock is perfect. Thank you!

lines.say: Lovely! You're booked for Wednesday at 3 PM.
lines.direction: Ava: warm, satisfied, reassuring — the payoff. A gentle smile on "Lovely."
lines.speak: Lovely! You're all booked for Wednesday at 3 PM. See you then!

lines.direction: Second caller (on the phone): curious, casual, friendly.
lines.speak: Quick question, do you do home visits?

lines.say: I don't have an answer for that, and I don't want to guess. I'll ask the team to call you back today.
lines.direction: Ava: honest and empathetic, never robotic — a hint of apology on "I don't want to guess", then confident and kind on "I'll ask the team to call you back today."
